sources.title: Peraturan Menteri Negara Lingkungan Hidup No. 13 Tahun 2009 tentang Baku Mutu Emisi Sumber Tidak Bergerak bagi Usaha dan/atau Kegiatan Minyak dan Gas Bumi
sources.scope: Gas turbines (Lampiran I, item 1.b). Its engine table is superseded by Permen LHK 11/2021 for engines/gensets and is not included here.

sources.title: Peraturan Menteri Lingkungan Hidup dan Kehutanan No. 11 Tahun 2021 tentang Baku Mutu Emisi Mesin dengan Pembakaran Dalam (Genset)

groups.basisNote: Footnote read from PDF: corrected to 15 % O2, dry; gas volume at 25 degC and 1 atm.
notes: There is no CO limit in this table. Any CO limit for a turbine comes from a site permit or an OEM guarantee, not from this regulation.

Presenter's database note: many turbine monitoring points only require NOx. Particulate is exempted for unit capacity below 25 MW. SO2 is exempted when routine fuel-gas sulfur is below 0.5 % by weight. Confirm against the regulation text.

groups.basisNote: Footnote read from PDF text (OCR quality is poor): all parameters corrected to 15 % O2; gas volume at 25 degC and 1 atm, dry. The correction formula in the annex uses 21 % as the ambient O2 term. Confirm the 15 % figure and the dry basis in the official text.
notes: Below 100 kW: under the threshold, no stack monitoring required (presenter's database note).

Per the PDF text (verify): monitoring is exempt for engines of 100 kW or less, engines running under 1,000 h cumulative per year, emergency/repair/maintenance use up to 200 h per year, and welding-set engines. Manual monitoring frequency: once every 3 years (101-500 kW), yearly (501-1000 kW), every 6 months (1001 kW and above).
Compliance deadline in the PDF text (verify): new limits apply no later than 1 May 2022.
